title: A sacrificial magnet concept for field dependent surface science studies
author: Liu, Oppliger, et al.

steps.title: Clean permanent magnets
steps.instruction: Rinse each NdFeB magnet sequentially with acetone followed by ethanol, then allow to dry before handling.

steps.title: Mount magnet on transfer tool
steps.instruction: Place the cleaned NdFeB magnet (10 × 3 × 2 mm³) onto the custom‑made transfer tool fabricated from Steel StW 22; the tool is already connected to the linear transporter used for sample transfer.

steps.title: Anneal sample without magnet
steps.instruction: Heat the sample on the magnetizable Steel StW 22 plate to the required preparation temperature (e.g., 577 °C for Au(111)) while the magnet is absent; the temperature may exceed the magnet’s Curie temperature (~400 °C).

steps.title: Attach magnet after cooling
steps.instruction: Once the sample temperature has dropped below the NdFeB Curie temperature (T < TC ≈ 400 °C), bring the transfer tool with the magnet into contact with the steel sample plate; because the contact‑area ratio AMT/AMS ≈ 1/5, the magnet preferentially adheres to the plate.

steps.title: Transfer plate into STM
steps.instruction: Move the steel plate with the attached NdFeB magnet into the low‑temperature STM (Createc system) for the magnetic‑field‑dependent experiment.

steps.title: Perform STM vortex measurement
steps.instruction: Place a NbSe₂ single crystal (Tc = 7.2 K) on the plate, cool to 4 K, and acquire dI/dV conductance maps at Vbias = 4 mV, I = 500 pA, Vmod = 2 mV, 887 Hz; record vortex lattice at four tip locations with distances L = 1.40 ± 0.08 mm, 1.62 ± 0.08 mm, 1.94 ± 0.08 mm, and 2.45 ± 0.08 mm from the magnet edge, obtaining mean vortex spacings dv = 100 ± 3 nm, 105 ± 4 nm, 113 ± 5 nm, and 128 ± 5 nm respectively.

steps.title: Calculate magnetic field from vortices
steps.instruction: Use the flux quantum Φ₀ = 2.068 × 10⁻¹⁵ T·m² and the triangular lattice relation B = 2Φ₀/(3 dv²) to convert each measured dv into a magnetic field (≈ 350 mT at the closest tip position down to ≈ 150 mT at the farthest).

steps.title: Simulate field with FEMM
steps.instruction: Model the steel sample plate (μr = μrFe) and the NdFeB magnet in FEMM; evaluate the out‑of‑plane field at 100 µm above the plate (matching the NbSe₂ thickness) and at 2 mm above the plate (typical substrate height). Include a temperature‑dependent reduction of up to 14 % near 135 K due to a 30° easy‑axis canting.

steps.title: Sacrifice magnet after experiment
steps.instruction: Re‑heat the sample plate with the attached magnet using the manipulator heater stage; rotate the manipulator so the magnet drops into a stainless‑steel collection basket once the temperature exceeds TC (~400 °C), thereby irreversibly demagnetizing the NdFeB magnet.

steps.title: Optional: redesign plate for field tailoring
steps.instruction: If higher fields are desired, modify the geometry of the Steel StW 22 plate (or use a non‑magnetic substrate, μr = 1) and repeat FEMM simulations; note that a magnetizable plate can boost flux density above 500 mT, while a non‑magnetic plate yields lower fields (dashed blue curve).
